Date: 2026-03-10
Time: 10:00 PT
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Morgan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), David Chen (Redwood SE), Evan Brooks (ClearPath SRE), Marta Ruiz (ClearPath ML), Samir Khan (ClearPath Product), Lisa Park (ClearPath Infra)
Shared artifacts: https://drive.company/clearpath/ttft-kernel-comparison.xlsx, https://redwood.app/playbooks/seqlen-kernel-playbook-v2.pdf
summary: Week 3 sync: reviewed latest TTFT/streaming numbers, sequencelength-driven kernel mapping, and a fallback/canary plan. Decided to favor kernel-B for short seqlen streaming path with hedged fallback to kernel-A for degraded tails. Agreed to a 5% canary followed by 25% if metrics hold. Action items assigned for playbook, replay, and security docs.
topics: TTFT changes after kernel swap; streaming handshake and KV cache interactions; sequence length thresholds (<=32, 33-128, >128); fallback and hedging playbook; canary rollout plan; cost/CPU tradeoffs; monitoring metrics (p50, p95, p99 TTFT, cpu%, kv-hit-rate)
transcript:
[00:00] Morgan Lee: okay everyone thanks for joining, this is our week three handoff for the pilot, we wanted to go over the numbers and land on a playbook for seqlen->kernel mapping.
[00:22] Evan Brooks: thanks Morgan, quick note, we've got a dev cluster with identical networking but only three gpus so expect a bit higher variance.
[00:35] Priya Nair: yep understood, we'll factor that in. quick recap: last week kernel-A was our baseline, kernel-B is the new fastpath for short sequences. on the sample traces we saw median TTFT drop from ~120ms to ~95ms on the 0-32 token bucket.
[01:05] Marta Ruiz: interesting — what about tails? we saw p99 go up last run on kernel-B, something about microbursts?
[01:18] David Chen: right, there was increased CPU contension in the runtime during streaming handshake spikes, that amplified the tail to ~280ms vs 230ms on kernel-A.
[01:35] Lisa Park: is that the KV cache warm cold effect or the kernel's scheduling?
[01:42] Priya Nair: a bit of both — the kernel-B micro-optimizations reduce per-token compute but are more sensitive to context-switching when the KV cache miss rate climbs. so if kv-hit-rate drops below ~92% we saw tail jitter.
[02:05] Samir Khan: so operationally what do we do? route short requests to B, long to A, and if kv misses spike flip back?
[02:15] Morgan Lee: yes that's the idea. our proposed playbook: seqlen <=32 -> kernel-B fastpath; 33-128 -> kernel-hybrid (staged batching on A kernels with quantized ops); >128 -> kernel-A baseline. plus a hedging rule: if p95 TTFT increases by >20% over baseline for more than two minutes, trigger immediate fallback to kernel-A for that route and open an incident.
[02:45] Evan Brooks: what about streaming partial responses? we can't introduce a big latency hiccup when switching mid-stream.
[02:55] Priya Nair: we avoid mid-stream kernel swaps; hedging happens at request admission. for active streams we use a warm-standby fallback — duplicate only the next token batch to kernel-A in rare cases, but that's opt-in. it's heavier on tokens but keeps first-byte stable.
[03:20] Marta Ruiz: hmm duplication sounds costly. any numbers?
[03:25] David Chen: rough estimate: duplication adds 1.3x token cost on duplicated batches but reduces mean tail by ~40ms on our corp dev traces. we'll include exact calc in the spreadsheet.
[03:45] [00:04:00] Morgan Lee: moving to the numbers we ran last night — hoping to be pragmatic. p50/p95/p99 for conversation baseline (kernel-A): 120/210/370 ms; kernel-B short path: 95/240/420 ms — so better median, worse tail.
[04:15] Evan Brooks: that's consistent with our signaled spikes when our synthetic microbursts run.
[04:30] Priya Nair: we also tested enabling persistent KV cache across requests which moved kernel-B p99 down to ~320ms in the best runs, so caching is a big lever.
[04:50] Lisa Park: KV cache durability in our infra is a question — we have intermittent pod restarts during deploys. does Redwood support fast KV warm reloads?
[05:02] Morgan Lee: yes we have a warm restore handshake; it can prefetch top-k keys during pod startup. charted perf is in the drive link.
[05:15] Samir Khan: timeline wise are we comfortable with a 5% canary next week?
[05:22] Morgan Lee: propose 5% on Monday 2026-03-22 for 24h then evaluate. metric gates: p95 not worse than +10% vs baseline, p99 not worse than +20% and error rate <0.1%.
[05:40] Marta Ruiz: who will own the gate checks?
[05:45] Evan Brooks: we'll own the telemetry, Redwood will instrument additional dashboards and alerts.
[06:00] Priya Nair: action: we'll deliver a condensed playbook that maps sequence length ranges to kernel choices, plus fallback thresholds and example alert rules.
[06:12] David Chen: also adding a recommended canary query set (approx 500 queries representing short, medium, long). we used a seeded replay for these.
[06:30] Marta Ruiz: quick note on cost: kernel-B runs ~8% cheaper per token in our tests but because of duplication hedging it could be net neutral for mixed traffic. we need the finance signal.
[06:45] Morgan Lee: noted, add finance to the loop if ROI is ambiguous after canary.
[06:52] [00:10:00] Evan Brooks: security/compliance — SSO and audit logs, we need the SAML assertion flow tested and logs retained 90 days for our compliance.
[07:05] Morgan Lee: yep we will share the SSO test checklist; Redwood supports SAML 2.0, SCIM provisioning, and audit logs can be exported to customer S3 or SIEM.
[07:22] Lisa Park: is there any PII touch by logs? we require redaction for request bodies.
[07:30] Priya Nair: by default we don't store full request bodies for hosted pilot; for dedicated we can configure request redaction and bring-your-own-key for KMS. we'll attach the security doc.
[07:45] Samir Khan: great. on monitoring, what exact dashboards will you add?
[07:52] David Chen: three dashboards: TTFT by route and kernel, KV hit/miss heatmap, and CPU/GPU contention over time. plus a canary-specific view that flags gate breaches.
[08:08] Marta Ruiz: sample alerts?
[08:10] Priya Nair: p95 > +10% for 2 successive 1-min windows -> pager; p99 > +20% for any single 1-min window -> urgent; kv-hit-rate <90% for 3 mins -> info alert.
[08:28] [00:15:00] Morgan Lee: okay let's talk about the replay Marta will run. Marta?
[08:35] Marta Ruiz: yes, we'll use our replay harness to push the 10k sample through dev cluster. question: should we enable persistent KV cache during replay or simulate cold starts?
[08:45] Priya Nair: do both. run two passes: coldstart (no prewarm) and warm path (prefetch keys). compare p99.
[09:00] Evan Brooks: we'll also enable jitter injection to mimic our burst patterns.
[09:08] David Chen: good. and please attach the raw logs and a small script to compute percentiles — we can help if needed.
[09:20] [00:20:00] Samir Khan: any blockers on the canary config? what about circuit breakers?
[09:26] Priya Nain: (slight mispronunciation) Priya Nair: we support circuit breakers on per-route basis, and will set an emergency global fallback if overall cluster p99 spikes >30% for 3 consecutive minutes.
[09:40] Lisa Park: rolling deploy concerns — if we lose a node during canary we might lose KV warm state and see transient tails. recommend a staggered canary aligned with deploy windows.
[09:55] Morgan Lee: agree. we'll coordinate canary during low deploy traffic and monitor.
[10:05] [00:25:00] Marta Ruiz: quick question about metrics ingestion — what's the expected cardinality? we need to map to our Prometheus schematics.
[10:15] David Chen: low cardinality: route, kernel, seqlen-bucket, pod-id. should be manageable.
[10:30] Evan Brooks: final question, competitors — Nimbus pitched an aggressive latency number but lacked streaming hedges, we should ensure our playbook emphasizes graceful degradation.
[10:42] Morgan Lee: yep we'll call that out in the playbook.
[10:50] [00:35:00] Priya Nair: recap of decisions: kernel-B short-path for <=32; hybrid for 33-128; kernel-A for >128; hedging fallback rules and duplication opt-in; KV caching is high leverage; 5% canary 2026-03-22 with metric gates; deliver playbook by 2026-03-12.
[11:12] Marta Ruiz: sounds good. one last thing — can we get the kernel binary diff or a summary of code-level changes?
[11:20] David Chen: we'll provide an ops-friendly changelog and perf notes, not the full source.
[11:28] Samir Khan: thanks all.
[11:30] Morgan Lee: thanks team, expect the playbook and spreadsheet this week.
[11:35] [00:54:00] (end)
